'''''Opuntia aurantiaca''''', commonly known as '''tiger-pear''', '''jointed cactus''' or '''jointed prickly-pear''', is a species of [[cactus]] from [[South America]].<ref name="GRIN"/> The species occurs naturally in [[Argentina]], [[Paraguay]] and [[Uruguay]] and is considered an [[invasive species]] in [[Africa]] and [[Australia]].<ref name="GRIN"/>

== Description ==
''Opuntia aurantiaca'' rarely exceeds 0.5 m in height (may reach 2 m with standing support). Plants consist of up to 100 or more cladodes from 5 to 20 cm long and 1 to 3 cm wide.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Bakewell-Stone |first=Petra |date=2024-09-10 |title=Opuntia aurantiaca (jointed cactus) |url=https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/full/10.1079/cabicompendium.37708 |journal=CABI Compendium |volume=CABI Compendium |article-number=37708 |doi=10.1079/cabicompendium.37708|doi-access=free }}</ref> 

== Distribution and habitat ==
This species' native is to Argentina ([[Buenos Aires Province|Buenos Aires]] and [[Entre Ríos Province|Entre Rios]]), Uruguay and Paraguay.<ref name=":0" />

== Invasive species ==
It was declared a [https://web.archive.org/web/20130601104627/http://www.weeds.org.au/WoNS/ Weed of National Significance] by the [https://web.archive.org/web/20130729002821/http://weeds.org.au/awc.htm Australian Weeds Committee] in April 2012, and was [http://www.weeds.org.au/cgi-bin/weedident.cgi?tpl=plant.tpl&ibra=all&card=S28 reported by the Committee] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304004154/http://www.weeds.org.au/cgi-bin/weedident.cgi?tpl=plant.tpl&ibra=all&card=S28 |date=2016-03-04 }} to be the most troublesome of all cactus species in [[New South Wales]] and the [[Invasive species in Australia|worst Opuntia species]] in [[Queensland]]. It is currently controlled biologically in Australia using the cochineal insect ''[[Dactylopius austrinus]]'', and to a lesser extent by the larvae of two moths, ''[[Cactoblastis cactorum]]'' and ''[[Tucumania tapiacola]]''.<ref name=":0" />
